name: Field House
use: Varsity athletics hub: Lundholm Gym (basketball, volleyball, gymnastics), Paul Sweet Oval indoor track, Swasey indoor pool

renovations.what: Henry 'Hank' C. Swasey indoor pool dedicated
Lundholm Gymnasium restoration approved Dec 2000; refinished floor, new bleachers, lighting, sound and scoreboards (dates of each not given)
Paul Sweet Oval indoor track renovation, funded by $266,000 from more than 125 alumni and friends

facts.text: Built in 1937; the Board of Trustees blocked a student push to rename it for William H. Cowell, keeping the name University of New Hampshire Field House.
Lundholm Gym, its main component, is named for Carl Lundholm, athletic director 1939–1963; it was renamed in 1968.
Lundholm seats about 2,500 (UNH events) to 3,000 (Wikipedia); its court was named Friel Court in 2008.
The fields outside are named Lewis Fields for Dr. Edward Morgan Lewis.

verdict: 1937 brick athletics hall whose Lundholm Gym and Swasey Pool are serviceable but old-school.
notes: Old row's additions (1966, 1988), Azumah Performance Center (2003/2019–20 $1.5M) and 1990s report quotes were NOT re-verified. Stadium Journey review date is approximate (mentions 2024–25 season). Wikipedia says Lundholm is 'attached to Wildcat Stadium' (in the Whittemore article). Photo: historic image shows a plain brick block with a pedimented parapet and press box above stadium bleachers; no modern exterior photo checked. Licensed photo (2013, interior): Lundholm Gym has a polished wood court, blue pull-out bleachers on one side, and a high wood-trussed roof with skylight strips; functional and a bit dated. No licensed exterior photo of the Field House found. Licensed interior added: a 2018 Flickr photo titled 'Swasey Pool' shows the competition pool with brick walls and a coffered ceiling.
judgeNotes: Interior photos show a trussed gym and a decent pool; exterior only from a historic photo. No licensed exterior, so the gym leads the gallery.
